lines.text: Your baby brain was recording memories, and you can't find a single one.
Most adults remember nothing from before about age three.
For decades, scientists thought baby brains simply couldn't store memories.
Then in 2025, Yale researchers scanned babies' brains while they looked at pictures.
When the memory center lit up brighter, the baby was more likely to recognize that picture later.
So the memories were being saved, in babies as young as one.
The real problem may be finding them again.
It's like a library where the books are on the shelves, but nobody can look them up.
Scientists are still testing how long baby memories last.
So somewhere inside you, your first birthday may still be saved.
